summary: 1979 WWII-surplus Army tower on a 1921 lookout site in Stanislaus County; lookouts named 1924-1938; now a private communications site, NHLR-registered 2019.

facts.design: World War II surplus Army observation tower brought from Tracy Airport, possibly an Aermotor product; cab altered for a catwalk and door
facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection

staffing.status: last named lookout 1938; not on CAL FIRE's June 2008 list

access.note: NHLR description dated October 1991 (MVT 10/91) says the site is not accessible to the public; Bay Area Peaks describes a private road to the summit

visit.trail_note: About 13 miles from paved road per the NHLR description (MVT 10/91); summit reached by a private road per Bay Area Peaks

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the earlier station closed in 1938, but a July 1938 newspaper item still names Paul Kraft as lookout. Any closure came later in 1938; no month is given.

NHLR says a second tower was erected in 1942; the 1980 Modesto Bee item says the new tower replaced one built in 1921. Both accounts are recorded; the sources do not say which earlier tower the 1979 tower replaced.

notes_for_editor: Brief said access 'unknown'; recorded as private from the NHLR description (dated October 1991) and Bay Area Peaks (undated). Brief's 1979 date for the existing tower confirmed; first lookout (1921) and 1942 tower added. thedirtymule.com (search snippet calls it an active lookout) returned 403 and was not used. Photo lead not added: archive.org item casbcfm_001080 (July 1953 construction photo) seen in search results; licence not checked.
